features.name: Small Language Models
features.description: Smaller AI models with fewer parameters (measured in billions) that can perform tasks comparable to large language models. Phi 4 has 14 billion parameters and outperforms GPT-3, runs on single GPU, and can even run on home computers. Approximately 10 times faster than larger models in generating responses.
caveats: Not as good at reasoning as larger models
Limited world knowledge
Slower when run on home graphics cards

features.name: Fine-tuning for Business Central
features.description: Specialized training technique that adjusts a pre-trained language model using examples from specific domains like invoice classification to chart of accounts. Allows LLMs to perform specialized tasks they weren't originally good at. Can be applied to smaller models as a cost-effective alternative to GPT-4.
caveats: Requires skills and is an involved process
Should only attempt after trying prompt engineering first
Risk of overfitting to training data - models may not generalize to different customer data with different master data
Requires varied data generation for production deployment beyond test scenarios

features.name: Model Distillation
features.description: Cost-saving technique where output from a larger model like GPT-4 is used to train a smaller model like GPT-4 mini to behave the same way. The larger model acts as the teacher and the smaller model as the student. Achieves 10-15x cost savings.
caveats: Requires the larger model to work well on the specific use case first

features.name: Phi Model Series
features.description: Microsoft's series of small language models released over time. Phi 1 had 1.3 billion parameters released a year and a half ago, and Phi 4 with 14 billion parameters was released in December. These models outperform GPT-3 and are on par with GPT-4 for many simple tasks.
caveats: Limited knowledge about world facts
Not ideal for tasks requiring reasoning

features.name: AI test toolkit
features.description: Framework for testing AI features using data-driven tests with AL assertions to verify AI agent behavior and accuracy metrics. Supports both AL-based assertions for structured output validation and LLM-based testing for natural language output quality.
caveats: requires careful data set management to avoid overfitting

features.name: Data generation for AI testing
features.description: Using LLMs to generate synthetic test data by taking seed examples and creating variations to build large test datasets for AI features.
caveats: requires careful seed data curation

features.name: Sales order agent
features.description: An agent that processes customer emails, generates sales quotes, and responds with generated emails. Features both AL-based assertions for quote validation and LLM-based testing for email quality. Uses execute task steps to control Business Central navigation.
features.status_evidence_quote: it's a feature which is in preview uh you we actually generate we have the LM generating a reply to the customer
caveats: relies on both AL-based and LLM-based validation
email generation quality must be validated

features.name: Execute task steps for agent control
features.description: Core functionality where the agent determines what to do next in Business Central, including deciding where to click and which fields to fill out based on LLM reasoning.
caveats: complex task requiring LLM training
accuracy varies significantly between models

features.name: GPT-4 Mini fine-tuning optimization
features.description: Fine-tuned GPT-4 Mini achieving over 90% accuracy on execute task steps, outperforming full GPT-4 while maintaining significantly lower costs. Fine-tuning uses successful test case runs as training data, extracting input-output pairs from execute task steps where the agent interacts with Business Central.
caveats: preliminary results
trained on limited data set
risk of overfitting to specific customer and item names
may not generalize to different customer datasets

features.name: Cost-accuracy tradeoff analysis
features.description: Comparison showing GPT-4 costs 22 cents for 10 emails at 85% accuracy, GPT-4 Mini costs 1 cent with 30% accuracy, and fine-tuned GPT-4 Mini achieves sweet spot with 90% accuracy at modest cost increase.
caveats: based on preliminary testing
costs may vary with scale

features.name: Prompt engineering for cost reduction
features.description: Recommendation to start with prompt engineering techniques like few-shot prompting and Chain of Thought before considering fine-tuning, as initial cost-saving step.

features.name: Data quality requirements for fine-tuning
features.description: Fine-tuning quality depends critically on having representative, accurate training data that is not reused in test sets to avoid overfitting. Good tooling exists in AI Foundry but data preparation is the main work.
caveats: Data generation for varied scenarios is challenging and resource-intensive
Avoiding overfitting requires careful separation of training and test data
